hero.title: Montreal Protocol and Kigali Agreement: UPSC Notes
hero.description: Comprehensive UPSC study notes covering the Vienna Convention (1985), Montreal Protocol (1987), Kigali Amendment (2016), HFC phase-down schedules, India's compliance timeline, and Prelims key facts.

timeline.title: Chronological Progression of Ozone & Climate Treaties
timeline.description: Key international milestones in ozone layer protection and greenhouse gas regulation.

cards.title: Vienna Convention
cards.details: Adopted as a framework convention for the protection of the Ozone Layer. Non-binding goals for research and data exchange.

cards.title: Montreal Protocol
cards.details: Signed on 16 September 1987 (World Ozone Day). Legally binding phase-out of Ozone Depleting Substances (ODSs) such as CFCs and Halons.

cards.title: Kigali Amendment
cards.details: Adopted in Kigali, Rwanda to amend the Montreal Protocol. Mandates the global phase-down of Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), potent greenhouse gases.

cards.title: Kigali Enters into Force
cards.details: Entered into force globally on January 1, 2019. Ratified by India in 2021 to phase down HFCs in four steps by 2047.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Memory Hacks
mnemonics.description: Memory triggers to help retain this topic for UPSC Prelims.

items.label: India HFC Baseline Year
items.text: India's baseline is 2024-2026. Phase-down starts from 2028 with an 80% reduction by 2047.

items.correction: False! Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) have an Ozone Depletion Potential (ODP) of Zero. They were introduced as replacements for CFCs/HCFCs. However, they are super-potent greenhouse gases with Global Warming Potential (GWP) thousands of times higher than CO2.

items.trap: Montreal Protocol is non-binding like UNFCCC.
items.correction: False! The Montreal Protocol is the only universal UN treaty with 198 member states and legally binding timetables for both developed and developing countries.

sections.title: 1. The Montreal Protocol (1987)
sections.content:
Quick Overview: Kigali Agreement UPSC

The Kigali Amendment (2016) to the Montreal Protocol is a legally binding international agreement to phase down the production and consumption of Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) by 80-85% by the late 2040s. Phasing down HFCs is projected to prevent up to 0.5°C of global warming by 2100.

The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer was finalized in 1987 under the 1985 Vienna Convention. It is widely regarded as the most successful multilateral environmental agreement in history, achieving universal ratification (198 nations) and phasing out over 99% of controlled ozone-depleting substances.

  • Target Substances: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), Halons, Carbon Tetrachloride, Methyl Chloroform, Hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs).
  • Multilateral Fund (1991): Established to assist developing countries (Article 5 parties) in financial and technical transitions.
  • Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR): Developing and developed nations have distinct phase-out timelines.

sections.title: 2. The Kigali Amendment (2016)
sections.content:
In October 2016, at the 28th Meeting of Parties (MOP 28) in Kigali, Rwanda, parties agreed to amend the Montreal Protocol to include HFCs (Hydrofluorocarbons) under its ambit.

Why Amend Montreal Protocol for Climate Change?

HFCs are non-ozone-depleting chemicals developed to substitute CFCs/HCFCs in refrigeration, air-conditioning, and foam manufacturing. However, HFCs are potent greenhouse gases with global warming potentials (GWP) up to 12,000 times that of carbon dioxide ($CO_2$).

Group 1 (Developed)USA, EU, UK, Japan201986% by 2036
Group 2 (Developing - A)China, Brazil, South Africa202480% by 2045
Group 3 (Developing - B)India, Pakistan, Iran, Gulf States202885% by 2047

sections.title: 3. India's Commitment & Cooling Action Plan (ICAP)
sections.content:
The Union Cabinet of India ratified the Kigali Amendment in August 2021. India has formulated the India Cooling Action Plan (ICAP) in 2019—making India the first country in the world to launch a comprehensive document addressing cooling demand across sectors.

  • Cooling Demand Reduction: 20% to 25% reduction by 2037-38.
  • Refrigerant Demand Reduction: 25% to 30% reduction by 2037-38.
  • Energy Efficiency: Transition to climate-friendly alternatives while maximizing cooling efficiency.

practiceQuestions.q: The 'Kigali Amendment' to the Montreal Protocol, which entered into force in 2019, aims to achieve which of the following objectives?
options: A. Complete ban on single-use plastics by 2030
B. Phasing down the production and consumption of Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs)
C. Mandating carbon taxation on aviation emissions
D. Banning transboundary movement of electronic waste
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Kigali Amendment was adopted in 2016 to phase down Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), which are super-potent greenhouse gases with high Global Warming Potential (GWP).

practiceQuestions.q: Under the Kigali Amendment, India belongs to which compliance group and what is its phase-down start year?
practiceQuestions.explanation: India belongs to Article 5 Group 2 (often termed Group 3 alongside Gulf nations and Pakistan), where the baseline years are 2024-2026 and phase-down freeze begins in 2028, targeting an 85% cut by 2047.
